Plotting things side by side (iPython)

iPython doesn't render when exported to PDF. If you need to do this, use Matplotlib subplots instead.

from IPython.display import display
import ipywidgets as widgets

table_widget = widgets.Output()
with table_widget:
	display(chitable.style.applymap(highlight_sig, subset=["p"])) #display styled table


plot_widget = widgets.Output()
with plot_widget:
	sns.kdeplot(data=table["Asp1"],color='green') #display chart next to table
	sns.kdeplot(data=falsetable["Asp1"],color='red')
	plt.show()

display(widgets.HBox([table_widget,plot_widget]))

Auto plotting large numbers of figures

def assemble(param,fieldname):
	table=pd.DataFrame() #insert table here
	return(display(table.style.applymap(confstyle))) #display styled table
	
def plot_sbs(p,n):
	x=widgets.Output()
	with x:
		assemble(p,n)
	return x
	
display(widgets.HBox([
	plot_sbs("Ele1","Elevation"),
	plot_sbs("Asp1","Aspect"),
	plot_sbs("Slo1","Slope")]))

Plotting side by side (Matplotlib)


plt.subplot(1,6,1) #(total rows, total columns, plot on chart 1 of 6 this time)
plt.scatter(x,y)
plt.subplot(1,6,2) #(total rows, total columns, plot on chart 2 of 6 this time)
plt.scatter(x,y)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Plotting graphs with tables

plt.subplot(1,1,1)
plt.scatter(x,y)
cell_text=[]
for row in range(len(table)):
	cell_text.append(table.iloc[row])
plt.table(cellText=cell_text, colLabels=table.columns,bbox = [0, -1.3, 1, 1.3]) #bbox=[left, bottom, width, height]. This will plot the table under the graph

Figure numbering

Auto figure numbering for Jupyter notebooks

#paste this at the start
num = 1
table=1
eq=1

figures=[]
tables=[]
equations=[]

def fignum(ty,caption):

	global num
	global table
	global eq
	
	if ty == "table":
		print(f"Table {table}: {caption}")
		table = table + 1
	
	elif ty == "figure":
		print(f"Figure {num}: {caption}")
		num = num + 1
	
	elif ty== "eq":
		print(f"Equation {eq}: {caption}")
		eq = eq + 1

#then use before displaying a figure or table
fignum("table",f"Results of Chi Squared test")
display(chitable.style.applymap(highlight_sig, subset=["p"]))

Timelines

Plotly has a timeline function but it requires formatted dates and doesn't understand dates in BC. This code just uses basic integers.

dates=[{"Citation":"Pearson","Year":2023,"Min":-3000,"Max":-3000}, #dictionaries
		{"Citation":"Thorpe","Year":1991,"Min":-3100,"Max":2100}]
datetable=pd.DataFrame(dates) #convert to dataframe
  

min=datetable["Min"]
max=datetable["Max"]
year=datetable["Year"]
cit=datetable["Citation"]

plt.scatter(min,year,color="black") #make scatter plots
plt.scatter(max,year,color="black")

  
for i,txt in enumerate(cit):
	plt.annotate(txt, (min[i]+1, year[i]+1)) #label points with text

plt.plot([min,max], #plot lines
		[year,year],
		color="black")

plt.xlabel("Proposed arrival of the Welsh Bluestones at Stonehenge")
plt.ylabel("Year of Publication")
plt.show()
